description: A false-colour satellite image from Spot 5 (2.5 m resolution, 1/2/3 band combination), dated 2011-08-01, depicts the marshes and estuary of the Guadalquivir river within the Doñana Natura 2000 (N2K) site in Spain. The image shows a coastal landscape with distinct land cover types. The river and estuary appear as dark blue water bodies, particularly a winding river on the upper left and a larger body of water to the far right (likely the Atlantic Ocean). Extensive areas of vegetation, characteristic of marshes with salt-tolerant plants or reeds, are rendered in bright magenta/red, dominating the left side of the image and surrounding other features. In the central and upper-right portions, geometrically regular, lighter-toned rectangular plots are visible, consistent with agricultural fields, potentially rice fields as suggested by the surrounding context. These fields appear light grey or beige, some showing internal linear patterns. A narrow strip of lighter, possibly sandy, coastline separates the land from the ocean on the right. The image attribution is CNES 2011©, Distribution Airbus DS/Spot Image.
